processes: Plotting a point on a grid
plainLanguageExplanation: A point marks one exact location in space. It has no length, no width, no height — no size at all. You draw a tiny dot to represent it, and you name it with a capital letter, like point A or point P. On a grid, every point has a position — you can plot point A at row 3, column 5. Points are the smallest building blocks of geometry: a line is a path of points, a segment joins two points, and an angle is two rays sharing a point called the vertex.

whyItMatters: Every map pin, every city coordinate, every corner of a triangle is a point. Understanding that a point is a location — not a thing with size — is the foundation for all of geometry.
didYouKnow: A dot you draw is always too big to be a real point — a true point has zero size, which is why it can exist in infinitely many places but you can never actually touch one.
compareReason: Students think of points as little dots with size — comparing a point with a line shows size versus pure location.
